subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main job of decomposers in nutrient cycling?
options: They break down dead organisms and release nutrients into the soil
They produce energy from the Sun
They prevent nutrients from entering the soil
They hunt and eat primary consumers
questions.explain: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil for plants to reuse.

questions.q: Ice cores are useful evidence for past climate because they:
options: Trap air bubbles recording past atmospheric gases and temperature
questions.explain: Air bubbles trapped in ice cores reveal past greenhouse gas levels and temperatures over thousands of years.

questions.q: Why are tropical rainforests so important for the global environment?
options: They store carbon and produce oxygen
They cool the planet by producing ice
They reflect sunlight back into space
questions.explain: Rainforests act as a carbon store and 'carbon sink', and their photosynthesis releases oxygen, helping regulate the climate.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, which of these is an abiotic component?
questions.explain: Abiotic means the non-living physical parts of an ecosystem, such as temperature, water, light and soil.

questions.q: In the rainforest, the few very tall trees that poke above the main canopy form the:
questions.explain: Emergents are the tallest trees, sometimes over 45m, that rise above the continuous canopy to reach maximum sunlight.

questions.q: How is an Arctic fox adapted to a cold environment?
options: Long limbs and large ears to lose heat
Thick white fur for warmth and camouflage in snow
Brightly coloured fur to attract a mate
A thin coat to release heat
questions.explain: The Arctic fox has thick fur for insulation that turns white in winter for camouflage, plus small ears to reduce heat loss.

questions.q: The middle-latitude atmospheric circulation cell, between the Hadley and Polar cells, is the:
questions.explain: The Ferrel cell operates at mid-latitudes between the Hadley and Polar cells.

questions.q: Tropical storms generally do NOT form right at the equator because:
options: There is too little Coriolis effect to make them spin
The sea is too warm there
questions.explain: The Coriolis effect is near zero at the equator, so storms cannot start spinning.

questions.q: A large ecosystem covering a wide area, such as tropical rainforest or tundra, is called a:
questions.explain: A biome is a very large-scale ecosystem, such as desert or rainforest, defined mainly by its climate and vegetation.

questions.q: Hot deserts are best described as having:
options: Low rainfall and large daily temperature ranges
Constant cloud cover and high humidity
questions.explain: Hot deserts receive very little rain (under 250mm a year) and have hot days but cold nights, giving a large daily temperature range.

questions.q: Which is a PRIMARY effect of a tropical storm?
options: Buildings destroyed directly by strong winds
Disease spreading from contaminated water afterwards
Loss of tourism income months later
questions.explain: Wind damage to buildings happens directly during the storm, making it a primary effect.

questions.q: Which is an example of PLANNING to reduce tropical storm impacts?
options: Educating people on evacuation routes and storm drills
questions.explain: Preparation such as evacuation plans and public education reduces casualties when storms strike.

questions.q: Which is an example of MITIGATION of climate change rather than adaptation?
options: Switching to renewable energy to cut emissions
questions.explain: Mitigation reduces the causes (emissions); adaptation copes with the effects.

questions.q: Surface winds blowing towards the equator from the high-pressure belts are called the:
questions.explain: Trade winds blow from the subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equatorial low.

questions.q: Which condition is REQUIRED for a tropical storm to form?
options: Sea-surface temperatures of at least about 27 degrees C
questions.explain: Tropical storms need warm ocean water of around 27 degrees C or more to provide energy.

questions.q: How are plants such as lianas and epiphytes adapted to life in the rainforest?
options: They store fat to survive droughts
They climb or grow on other trees to reach sunlight
They lose their leaves in winter
They have thick fur to keep warm
questions.explain: Lianas climb up tree trunks and epiphytes grow on branches, both reaching the light without making their own tall trunks.

questions.q: Which human activity is a major threat to global biodiversity?
questions.explain: Destroying habitats removes the homes of plants and animals, reducing the variety of life (biodiversity).

questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is best described as a:
questions.explain: A herbivore is a primary consumer that feeds only on plants (producers).

questions.q: Why do many tall rainforest trees have buttress roots?
options: To support their height in thin, shallow soils
To reach sunlight at the forest floor
questions.explain: Buttress roots are large above-ground roots that give tall trees extra stability in the rainforest's thin, nutrient-poor soils.

questions.q: An example of an extreme UK weather hazard is:
options: Heavy snow, flooding and winter storms
A tropical cyclone forming over Britain
questions.explain: The UK experiences hazards such as flooding, storms, heatwaves and heavy snow.

questions.q: The Saffir-Simpson scale is used to measure the:
options: Strength of tropical storms by wind speed
questions.explain: The Saffir-Simpson scale rates tropical storms from category 1 to 5 by their wind speeds.

questions.q: Many scientists predict climate change will make tropical storms:
options: Move towards the poles and stop
questions.explain: Warmer oceans give storms more energy, so they are expected to become more intense.
